root_cause.text: In f2fs `check_swap_activate()`, the extent-handling logic misused `nr_pblocks == 0` after section-rounding of an unaligned swapfile extent to infer “last extent,” so tail migration skipped remapping/retrying and left later fragmented extents unmapped in `swap_extent`.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE and patch state that when `roundup(nr_pblocks, blks_per_sec)` exceeds `sis->max`, subtracting `blks_per_sec` makes `nr_pblocks = 0`; the old code then set `last_extent = true` and only retried `goto retry` when `!last_extent`, while the fix moves `last_extent` outside the block and unconditionally does `goto retry` after migration with the comment “lookup block mapping info after block migration.”

intent_record.intent_summary: Add a per-iteration `last_extent` flag in `check_swap_activate()` so retry logic can correctly track final-extent state within each loop pass.
intent_record.what: A new local boolean variable `last_extent` is declared and initialized to `false` inside the `while` loop, immediately before the `retry:` label in `check_swap_activate()`.
intent_record.how: This adds per-iteration state storage for tracking whether the current mapping/extent is the last one, with the value reset on each loop iteration; by placing it before the `retry:` label, the variable remains available across jumps to `retry` within the same iteration.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix swap activation extent validation so the last extent is excluded from the alignment/sequential-zone rejection path.
intent_record.what: The condition on the alignment/sequential-zone check was changed to include a new leading guard `!last_extent`, and the local declaration and initialization `bool last_extent = false;` was removed from inside that `if` block.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the misalignment handling path now executes only when the current extent is not the last extent, instead of always evaluating true for the removed local `last_extent` variable. This prevents the final extent from being treated as a misaligned/non-usable extent under those conditions and avoids unnecessary `not_aligned` accounting and block rounding for that case.

intent_record.intent_summary: Always retry block mapping lookup after block migration so swap activation does not proceed with stale extent information.
intent_record.what: The conditional check `if (!last_extent) goto retry;` was removed and replaced with an unconditional `goto retry;` at the point where block migration is detected, along with a new comment stating `lookup block mapping info after block migration`.
intent_record.how: After detecting block migration, the code now always retries block mapping lookup instead of retrying only when `last_extent` is null. This ensures mapping information is refreshed after migration in all cases, avoiding continued execution with potentially stale extent state.

consistency_review.core_intent: Fix swap activation extent validation by correctly tracking the final extent during iteration so last-extent handling bypasses inappropriate alignment/sequential-zone rejection.

relevance_review.reason: The changes directly fix the root cause in check_swap_activate(): they stop using extent state implied by nr_pblocks/iteration side effects to identify the final extent, add explicit last-extent tracking, and ensure last-extent handling avoids the incorrect rejection/retry path that caused later extents to remain unmapped.

The vulnerability is caused by skipping remapping/retrying after migrating an unaligned extent, which leaves later extents unmapped due to stale extent state. This group directly fixes that by always retrying block mapping lookup after migration.

candidates.rationale: The root cause is that extent logic later relied on nr_pblocks == 0 after section-rounding to infer the final extent. This rounding statement can transform the remaining length calculation so the code misclassifies an unaligned extent as the last extent, leading to skipped remap/retry and unmapped later extents.

This retry decision depended on the last_extent state computed in the buggy logic. Because last_extent was inferred incorrectly from nr_pblocks after rounding, this condition could suppress retry for a non-final extent, leaving subsequent fragmented extents unmapped.

Retrying block mapping after migration was necessary to avoid proceeding with stale extent information. In the vulnerable code path this retry was skipped when last_extent was misdetected, directly enabling the bad swap_extent state.

vuln_statements.explanation: This section-rounding changed nr_pblocks before later logic used nr_pblocks == 0 to infer whether the current swap extent was the last one. That misclassification of a non-final unaligned extent as the last extent is the root cause described.

This conditional guarded whether block mapping lookup would be retried after migration. Because last_extent could be computed incorrectly from the rounded nr_pblocks state, this check could wrongly suppress the retry for a non-final extent.
This retry path was skipped when the buggy last_extent state incorrectly indicated the extent was final. Skipping this remap/retry step let later fragmented extents remain unmapped in swap_extent.

bic_trace_step.reason: The provided function body for `check_swap_activate()` shows the relevant extent-handling logic clearly enough to decide. The vulnerable construct is present in the newly added unaligned-extent path. Specifically, after detecting misalignment with `if ((pblock - SM_I(sbi)->main_blkaddr) & sec_blks_mask || nr_pblocks & sec_blks_mask)`, the code rounds the extent length up: `nr_pblocks = roundup(nr_pblocks, blks_per_sec);` and then reduces it if it would exceed `sis->max`: `if (cur_lblock + nr_pblocks > sis->max) nr_pblocks -= blks_per_sec;`. It then uses `if (!nr_pblocks) { /* this extent is last one */ nr_pblocks = map.m_len; f2fs_warn(...); goto next; }`. This is exactly the root-cause pattern described: using `nr_pblocks == 0` after section-rounding/adjustment to infer that the current extent is the last one. That inference is unsafe because `nr_pblocks` can become 0 merely due to the round-up followed by subtraction on an unaligned extent near `sis->max`, not because there are no later fragmented extents. In that case the code skips `f2fs_migrate_blocks(...)` and jumps to `next`, so it does not remap/retry (`goto retry`) for that tail region, allowing later extents to remain unmapped in `swap_extent`. Therefore the vulnerable logic is present (`has_bug=true`). The fix is not present because the code still relies on `if (!nr_pblocks) { /* this extent is last one */ ... goto next; }` rather than correctly determining whether this is truly the final extent and retrying/remapping as needed. Hence `is_fixed=false`.

Author: Chao Yu <chao@kernel.org>
Date:   Mon Oct 12 17:06:05 2020 +0800

    f2fs: introduce check_swap_activate_fast()
    
    check_swap_activate() will lookup block mapping via bmap() one by one, so
    its performance is very bad, this patch introduces check_swap_activate_fast()
    to use f2fs_fiemap() to boost this process, since f2fs_fiemap() will lookup

    sign
bic_trace_step.reason: The provided snippet is sufficient because it shows the full newly introduced function `check_swap_activate_fast()` and the call site in `check_swap_activate()`. The stated root cause is a specific misuse of `nr_pblocks == 0` after section-rounding of an unaligned extent to infer the last extent, causing tail migration/remapping to be skipped. That vulnerable construct is not present in this commit's shown code. In `check_swap_activate_fast()`, `nr_pblocks` is derived from `map_bh.b_size` via `nr_pblocks = logical_to_blk(inode, map_bh.b_size);` and only capped by `if (cur_lblock + nr_pblocks >= sis->max) nr_pblocks = sis->max - cur_lblock;`. There is no logic that tests `nr_pblocks == 0`, no section-rounding handling, and no tail migration/remap/retry path at all. The function simply maps extents and calls `add_swap_extent(sis, cur_lblock, nr_pblocks, pblock)`. Therefore the vulnerable construct described in the root cause is absent here, so `has_bug` is false. Likewise, because the specific corrective handling for that later bug is also not present in this snippet, `is_fixed` is false.
